creatorProfiles.tagline: Food and product content that makes people hungry to buy

creatorProfiles.tagline: Product films and customer stories for software teams
creatorProfiles.bio: I make product walkthroughs, launch films, and customer story videos for B2B software companies. Former in-house video lead at a scheduling platform, so I write to the roadmap as much as to the camera. Remote-friendly workflow with scripted storyboards before every shoot.

creatorProfiles.tagline: Beauty and fashion campaigns with editorial polish

creatorProfiles.tagline: Training and equipment video for fitness brands

creatorProfiles.tagline: Destination and hospitality photography, Nordic to Mediterranean

contentRequests.title: 20 seasonal menu photos for our autumn dinner service
contentRequests.description: We are refreshing the autumn menu across all six locations and need photography for the printed menu, the website, and organic social. Shooting happens in our Portland kitchen over one service. We will have the full dish list, plating notes, and our own tableware ready on the day.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Warm, natural light with visible texture. Muted greens and warm neutrals. No heavy colour grading, no synthetic-looking food.
contentRequests.dos: Shoot each dish overhead and at 45 degrees. Include two or three wider table scenes. Leave headroom for menu typography.
contentRequests.donts: No stock props we do not own, no visible branding from other restaurants, no heavy vignettes.

contentRequests.title: Three 30-second class promo videos for the January membership push
contentRequests.description: We need three vertical promo videos covering strength, conditioning, and mobility classes, filmed at our Manchester studio. Members and coaches have already signed appearance releases. Captions are required because most of the placement is sound-off.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: High energy but never intimidating. Show a range of ages and abilities. Brand blue only as an accent, never as a full-frame wash.
contentRequests.dos: Open on movement in the first second. Include coach-to-member interaction. Burn in captions and end on the membership offer card.
contentRequests.donts: No before-and-after body comparisons, no calorie or weight-loss claims, no music that needs a separate licence.

contentRequests.title: Photo and video package for a new Douro Valley itinerary
contentRequests.description: We are launching a four-day Douro Valley trip and need a content package covering the vineyard stays, river section, and two partner restaurants. You would travel with the first departure group. Travel, accommodation, and meals are covered separately from the quoted fee.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Unhurried and warm. Real guests rather than staged models. Landscape frames must leave space for our itinerary overlay on the left third.
contentRequests.dos: Deliver a hero film plus vertical cutdowns. Cover mornings and golden hour. Photograph rooms empty and in use.
contentRequests.donts: No drone footage over the restricted vineyard zones, no partner logos in the hero film, no identifiable guests without a signed release.

contentRequests.title: 60-second evening routine explainer for a retinol serum launch
contentRequests.description: A single explainer video walking through a three-step evening routine with our new retinol serum. We supply product, packaging, and the approved claims list. The presenter should be comfortable talking to camera and reading from an autocue.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Soft daylight, clean bathroom set, minimal props. Copy on screen must match the approved claims list exactly.
contentRequests.dos: Show the pump and texture clearly. Keep each step under fifteen seconds. Include the patch-test reminder card at the end.
contentRequests.donts: No medical or clinical claims, no competitor products in frame, no filters that alter skin texture.

contentRequests.title: Two-minute product walkthrough for our shift scheduling release
contentRequests.description: We need a walkthrough film for the new scheduling release, aimed at operations managers evaluating us for the first time. We provide a demo environment with seeded data, the release notes, and a script outline. Screen capture plus light motion graphics, no on-camera presenter required.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Product-first. Interface recordings at full resolution, callouts in brand ink and teal, voiceover calm and unhurried.
contentRequests.dos: Follow the script outline. Record at 2560 by 1440 and deliver a 1080p master. Include an open-caption version.
contentRequests.donts: No customer names or real employee data on screen, no stock office footage, no claims about competitor products.

contentRequests.title: Listing photography for the spring bench tool range
contentRequests.description: Draft brief for the spring range: twelve SKUs needing white-background cutouts plus one in-use frame each. Still confirming which SKUs make the launch window, so quantities may change before we publish this.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Neutral grey backdrop for in-use frames, pure white for cutouts. Consistent scale across the range.
contentRequests.dos: Match the existing catalogue template. Keep shadows soft and consistent.
contentRequests.donts: No lifestyle staging, no props that imply a use case we do not support.

contentRequests.title: Launch photography for the new Portland location
contentRequests.description: We open our seventh site in Portland this autumn and need photography for the announcement: the dining room, the open kitchen, and a handful of signature dishes. Shooting before service on a quiet weekday. Everything is ready except the opening date, which is why this is still a draft.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Warm and unhurried, matching the autumn menu set. Natural light wherever possible, no flash in the dining room.
contentRequests.dos: Photograph the room empty and in use. Include the open kitchen pass. Leave headroom for the announcement overlay.
contentRequests.donts: No staff faces without a signed release, no competitor branding, no heavy colour grading.

contentRequests.title: Supplier farm visits — short films, details still to confirm
contentRequests.description: Rough notes for a series about the farms we buy from. We know we want three or four short films shot on location across the season, but the farms, the travel days, and the budget are all still being agreed internally.

contentRequests.title: Styled room sets for the compact sofa collection
contentRequests.description: Early draft for the compact sofa launch. We want three styled room sets and a short assembly film, but the delivery date depends on when the sample units clear customs.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Small-space realism. Rooms should read as apartments, not showrooms. Warm neutrals with one accent colour per set.
contentRequests.dos: Show scale against everyday objects. Include at least one frame per set with a person seated.
contentRequests.donts: No oversized rooms, no props from competitor brands.

contentRequests.title: Seasonal gift box photography for a limited spring range
contentRequests.description: We needed gift box photography for a limited spring range. The range sold out before the campaign went live, so we closed the brief without awarding it. Thank you to everyone who proposed.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Tactile and warm. Chocolate should read glossy, never melted or dull.
contentRequests.dos: Photograph boxes closed, open, and part-unwrapped.
contentRequests.donts: No seasonal props beyond the ones we supply.

contentRequests.title: 15 lifestyle photos for a single-origin gift box launch
contentRequests.description: Lifestyle photography for our new single-origin gift box, for use on the storefront and in paid social through the gifting season. We will ship product and packaging ahead of the shoot.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Warm, tactile, close focus. Deep browns with a single warm highlight. Hands in frame are welcome.
contentRequests.dos: Include three frames with the box closed and branding fully legible. Deliver square and 4:5 crops.
contentRequests.donts: No melted or broken product, no competitor packaging in frame.

contentRequests.title: Equipment demonstration films for six new studio machines
contentRequests.description: Six short demonstration films covering setup, correct form, and a common mistake for each new machine. These play on the studio screens and in the member app.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Clear, instructional, well-lit. One coach on camera throughout for continuity.
contentRequests.dos: Film each machine from front and side. Call out the safety stop in every film.
contentRequests.donts: No background music over the coaching audio, no members in frame without a release.

contentRequests.title: Texture and swatch photography for a new tinted SPF range
contentRequests.description: Swatch and texture photography across eight shades of our new tinted SPF, matched to the existing product page treatment so the range reads consistently.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Neutral white balance, no warming filters. Shade accuracy matters more than mood.
contentRequests.dos: Photograph swatches on a range of skin tones. Include one macro frame per shade.
contentRequests.donts: No retouching that alters shade colour, no props that cast coloured light.

contentRequests.title: Product photography for our autumn pastry range
contentRequests.description: Twelve photos of our autumn pastry range for the menu boards, our delivery listings, and social. Shooting happens in our Portland site before opening, and we will have every item plated and ready.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Warm natural light, visible texture, plain linen surfaces. Nothing over-styled — it should look like the counter.
contentRequests.dos: One overhead and one 45-degree frame per item. Leave square crops safe for delivery listings.
contentRequests.donts: No props we do not own, no heavy colour grading, no visible branding from other cafés.

contentRequests.title: Property photography for three partner hotels in the Algarve
contentRequests.description: Room categories, common areas, and breakfast service across three partner properties, shot over three days. Each property has agreed access windows and will hold rooms for you.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Bright and airy, true-to-life colour. Rooms must be photographed as guests find them.
contentRequests.dos: Shoot every room category. Include one exterior and one pool frame per property.
contentRequests.donts: No wide-angle distortion that oversells room size, no staff in frame without a release.

contentRequests.title: Three vertical reels for the autumn menu launch
contentRequests.description: Three vertical reels built around the autumn menu: one prep-led, one plating-led, and one dining room scene. These run on organic social during launch week.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Warm and hand-made. Kitchen noise is welcome in the mix. No voiceover.
contentRequests.dos: Open on motion. Keep cuts to the beat. Include the dish name as an on-screen caption.
contentRequests.donts: No trending audio that needs a commercial licence, no staff faces without a release.

contentRequests.title: Harvest supper club: a short film and a stills set
contentRequests.description: One evening of our harvest supper club, covered as a bundle: a short film for the events page and a small stills set for the newsletter. The room is candlelit and we would rather keep it that way than light it for camera.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Warm, low-light, unhurried. The room as guests actually experience it — no additional lighting rigs on the floor.
contentRequests.dos: Shoot the pass, the room, and two or three guest moments. Deliver the film and the stills matched in colour.
contentRequests.donts: No flash on the floor, no guest faces without a signed release, no staged plating.

contentRequests.title: Supplier market photography for the new sourcing page
contentRequests.description: A morning at the growers market with our head chef, photographed for the sourcing page we are adding to the site. Produce, hands, crates, and two or three portraits of the growers we buy from.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Early light, muted greens, visible texture. Documentary rather than styled.
contentRequests.dos: Shoot at the stalls rather than setting up a table. Include wide context frames as well as detail.
contentRequests.donts: No other traders’ branding in the foreground, no portraits without permission.

contentRequests.title: Catalogue photography for the modular shelving range
contentRequests.description: Catalogue photography for a modular shelving range in four finishes: each configuration styled and unstyled, plus joinery and hardware detail frames.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Calm, natural light, consistent camera height across configurations.
contentRequests.dos: Photograph each finish against the same backdrop. Include one detail frame per joint type.
contentRequests.donts: No mixed colour temperatures, no props taller than the shelving.

contentRequests.title: Feature explainer series for the reporting dashboard
contentRequests.description: A four-part explainer series covering the new reporting dashboard, for the help centre and in-product tours. Scripts are drafted; we need production, motion graphics, and captions.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Product-first with brand-ink callouts. Neutral narration, no background music bed under voiceover.
contentRequests.dos: Record from the demo environment we provide. Deliver caption files alongside each master.
contentRequests.donts: No real customer data on screen, no claims outside the release notes.

contentRequests.title: Demonstration films for the cordless multi-tool launch
contentRequests.description: Demonstration films for our cordless multi-tool: one overview film and three attachment-specific shorts, for listing pages and paid social.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Workshop-real, not staged. Show the tool doing actual work on real material.
contentRequests.dos: Include a close-up of each attachment changing over. Show correct protective equipment throughout.
contentRequests.donts: No unsafe technique on camera, no claims about run time that we have not verified.

contentRequests.title: App feature film for the connected training release
contentRequests.description: A single product film introducing the connected training features in our member app: screen capture, light motion graphics, and two short studio inserts.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Energetic but clear. App recordings must be legible at mobile size.
contentRequests.dos: Record the app at device resolution. Keep on-screen text above the safe area.
contentRequests.donts: No member data on screen, no music that needs a separate licence.

contentRequests.title: Campaign film for the barrier repair range relaunch
contentRequests.description: A 45-second campaign film for the barrier repair relaunch, plus vertical and square cutdowns for the launch week schedule.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Soft daylight, clean set, calm pacing. Copy on screen must match the approved claims list.
contentRequests.dos: Deliver 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1 masters. Include an open-caption version of each.
contentRequests.donts: No clinical claims, no filters that alter skin texture.

contentRequests.title: Villa and terrace photography for a summer stay collection
contentRequests.description: Photography for four villas joining the summer collection: interiors, terraces, and one twilight exterior each.
contentRequests.brandGuidelines: True-to-life colour, no oversaturated skies. Properties shot as guests find them.
contentRequests.dos: Include one twilight exterior per villa. Photograph every bedroom.
contentRequests.donts: No wide-angle distortion that oversells space, no neighbouring properties in frame.

contentRequests.title: Product photography for the single-origin truffle collection

contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Dark, warm, and tactile. Deep browns and brass, matte surfaces, one clear light source. Product-accurate colour above all — chocolate that photographs grey does not sell.
contentRequests.dos: Photograph each piece straight on and cut in half. Include three packaging scenes and one flat lay of the full collection.
contentRequests.donts: No melting or smearing for effect, no props we do not stock, no competitor packaging in frame.

contentRequests.title: Listing photography for the winter gift set range

contentRequests.brandGuidelines: Pure white background on the hero and angle frames, exactly as the marketplace spec requires. In-use frames on a workbench, natural light, no styling clutter.

contentRequests.donts: No composited shadows, no third-party tool brands in frame, no heavy retouching of tool marks.

contentRequests.title: Photo and video package for the winter tasting menu launch

contentRequests.donts: No stock props we do not own, no other restaurants’ branding in frame, no licensed music on the reels.

resolution.note: No deliverables were submitted and the creator did not respond to either party inside the review window. The payment has been refunded to the buyer in full and the account has been referred for a separate review.

disputes.description: The villa set is good work overall, but two bedrooms at the third property are missing entirely and the brief asked for every bedroom. We would like a partial adjustment rather than a re-shoot, since the collection is already live.

resolution.note: The delivery covers the agreed scope apart from two bedrooms that were occupied on the shoot day, which the creator noted at handover. A quarter of the order value has been returned to the buyer and the balance released to the creator. Both parties accepted this outcome.

disputes.description: The storefront frame looks softer than the rest of the set and we are not sure it is usable at print size. Raising this to get a second opinion before we accept the delivery.

resolution.note: The delivered files are sharp at full resolution; the softness the buyer saw came from the preview render rather than the masters. The delivery meets the brief, so the payment has been released to the creator in full.

disputes.description: The brief asked for every course as it is served across the eight-course menu and we have received eleven usable frames covering six courses. Two courses are missing entirely and the room frames were taken before the table was dressed, so none of them show service as it looks on the night.

Two of the three films arrived and the third has not been submitted at all. The two we do have were shot with the heaters off, so the courtyard reads cold and empty — which is the opposite of what the winter terrace campaign needs. We are due to launch the terrace in a fortnight.

Nothing has been submitted sixteen days past the delivery date and the brochure goes to print at the end of the month. The creator has answered here but we still have no files and no firm date, and we cannot hold the print slot any longer.

resolution.note: The creator corrected the wording on every master inside a day of being told, and the delivered files match the approved claims list supplied with the brief. disputeMessages.body: Opening this because we are three weeks past the delivery date with no files and no update. We are happy to extend if there is a genuine reason, but we need to hear something today.

The order specifies four films and three arrived. We would like the fourth delivered or the price adjusted to reflect three of four deliverables.

The sample tool shipped without the plunge head, so there was nothing to film for the fourth short. I raised it in the order thread on the shoot day and offered to film it as soon as the part arrives, at no extra cost.

Thank you both. I have the order thread and the delivery in front of me. Craftware, can you confirm when the plunge head is expected? If it lands inside a week, finishing the fourth film is the cleanest outcome for everyone.

Internal: order thread confirms the creator flagged the missing part on the shoot day, so this reads as a supply issue rather than a scope failure. Holding for the buyer to confirm the part date before proposing a partial release.
Nothing has been delivered and we have had no reply in the order thread since the shoot was booked. We need the funds back so we can re-post the brief.
Thank you for the detail. I have contacted the creator directly and opened a five-day window for a response before we decide.

Internal: no response from the creator across two contact attempts, and the same pattern appears on an unrelated licensing report. Refunding in full and referring the account to the accounts review queue.
Resolved in the buyer’s favour. The full amount has been returned to your payment method and should settle within three working days. Thank you for your patience.
Two bedrooms at the third villa are not in the set. Everything else meets the brief and we are already using it, so a re-shoot is not practical — a partial adjustment would settle this for us.
Both rooms were occupied on the day and the property would not move the guests. I flagged it in the delivery note at handover. I am happy with a proportionate adjustment rather than travelling back.

Internal: delivery note does record the occupied rooms, so this is a partial-scope shortfall rather than a quality failure. Both parties have proposed the same remedy — settling at a quarter of order value.
Resolved by agreement: a quarter of the order value returns to the buyer and the remainder is released to the creator. Thank you both for working this through so constructively.
The storefront frame looks soft to us at 100 per cent. Everything else in the set is excellent — we would just like this checked before we sign off.
Happy to have it checked. The master is 45 megapixels and sharp at full size — the file in the preview panel is a compressed proxy, which is likely what you are seeing.
Internal: downloaded the master and inspected at 100 per cent. Focus is on the storefront glazing as intended and the file is print-ready. No fault with the delivery.
Reviewed and closed in the creator’s favour. The master files are sharp at full resolution — the softness came from the compressed preview. Payment has been released and the order is complete.

Six of the eight courses are covered and the room frames were shot before we dressed the table. We would like the two missing courses photographed on a Friday service, or the price adjusted to reflect what arrived.

Both missing courses were pulled from the menu on the second night and I was told at the pass that they would not be going out. I am happy to come back for a third service at no extra cost once they are back on.

Internal: delivery note does mention two courses being pulled, so this looks like a menu change rather than a shortfall. Asking the buyer to confirm before proposing that the creator returns for one service.

Thank you both. Verde — can you confirm whether those two courses are back on the Friday menu, and whether a return visit works for you? If it does, that is the cleanest outcome here and the creator has already offered it at no charge.

The two films we have look like an empty courtyard on a cold night. The brief asked for the space at dusk with the heaters lit, and that is the whole point of the campaign. The third film has not arrived at all.

Thank you — I have watched both cuts against the brief. The heaters are visibly off in each one, and the brief does call for them lit. Ava, could you let us know whether a reshoot at dusk is possible, and by when?
Internal: brief is explicit about the heaters and the delivery note does not flag them as unavailable. Holding for the creator; if a reshoot is offered inside a week this closes without a refund.
We are sixteen days past the date with nothing delivered. The spring brochure goes to print at the end of the month and this property is four spreads of it.

The resort moved my access twice and then closed the terrace for resurfacing during my window. I have the rooms and both restaurants shot and can deliver those now, but the frontage and the terrace need a second visit.

Thank you both. A partial delivery of what is already shot is worth having while we work out the rest — Mateo, please submit those on the order. I am asking a senior reviewer to look at how the remainder should be settled given the print deadline.

Internal: escalating. Access was genuinely obstructed by the property, so this is not a creator failure, but the buyer loses the print slot either way. Likely landing on a partial release once the shot material is submitted.

The closing card on the first cut said "repairs the skin barrier" and our approved wording is "supports the skin barrier". We asked for it to be changed, but we want the delivered files checked against the approved list before we accept.
Updated masters went out the next morning with the approved wording on all three ratios and the caption files. Happy for them to be checked line by line against the list.

Reviewed and resolved. The delivered masters match the approved claims list, and the wording was corrected within a day of being raised. The payment has been released to the creator in full. Thank you for flagging it before accepting — that is exactly the right order to do it in.

reviews.comment: Liam wrote to our release notes, not just to the camera. The walkthrough needed one small wording change and nothing else, and the open-caption version was ready the same day.
Shade accuracy was spot on across all eighteen frames, which is the whole job with a serum launch. Dropped straight into the product pages with no re-grading.
Good energy in all three promos and the coaching cues are clear. Delivery ran a day past the agreed date, but Diego flagged it early and we still made the schedule.
Isla travelled with the group for five days and came back with a set we are still using across brochures and social. Every frame leaves room for our itinerary overlay, exactly as briefed.
Beautifully calm room sets that make a small bedroom read generously without exaggerating it. Yuki styled on set and saved us a separate stylist fee.
Amara turned two days of booth footage into a recap film our sales team actually sends to prospects. Fast, professional, and easy to brief.
Lovely natural light on the refill range and the sequence frames explain the product well. A couple of frames needed a straighten, handled within the revision round.
Three reels, all under the length limit, all captioned correctly, delivered a day early. Ava knows how a kitchen works and never got in the way of service.
Clear, well-paced explainers that our new members actually finish. We would have liked one more variation for the app tour, but that was outside the agreed scope.
Two guesthouses covered in a single trip with consistent light across both. Isla is the first person we call for property work now.
The demonstration films do the job and the safety equipment is visible throughout, which matters to us. Audio needed a pass in the second film.
Consistent camera height across twenty-six frames made the catalogue refresh painless. One finish needed a re-grade, turned around quickly.
The hamper range has never looked better. Warm, tactile, and the closed-box frames keep our branding fully legible for the storefront.
Our customer was comfortable on camera within minutes, which is most of the battle with a story film. The final cut has been our best-performing page asset this quarter.
Well produced and fully compliant with our claims list. The pacing in the middle section runs slightly long for paid social, so we trimmed it in-house.
The finished frames are good, but the delivery arrived at the end of the agreed window with little communication in between. The work itself met the brief.
Diego filmed four machines in one session and the form on camera is correct in every clip. Our coaches signed these off without a single note.
Thirty-five usable frames from a single showcase day, including partner stands and genuine guest moments. Releases were handled without us having to ask.
Twenty SKUs shot to the same template, so the accessory range finally reads as one family on the listing pages. Exactly what we needed.
Sara scripted, presented, and edited the whole onboarding set. New kitchen staff now watch five short films instead of reading a folder, and it shows.
Sharp teaser and delivered ahead of the launch date. We asked for a second edit late in the process and that sat outside the revision allowance, fairly enough.
Great coverage of the opening night and the queue-outside-the-door shot is now our hero image. A few frames were softer than the rest of the set.
Every piece in the range was shot to the same table height and light, so the product grid finally looks like one collection instead of twenty-two separate listings.
The counter films look and sound great, and the vertical cuts were sized correctly first time. We needed one extra pass on the pricing overlay, handled inside the revision round.
Ava spent the morning at the market with our chef and came back with a set that tells the sourcing story on its own. The supplier page barely needs copy now.

The final frames are clean and the cutouts are exactly to spec. Scheduling took longer than we expected and two rounds of emails went unanswered over a weekend, which is the only reason this is not higher.
Amara covered a full supper club service without a single guest noticing a camera. We had the first edit of the gallery two days later and it is already running across the harvest series pages.
Lovely produce frames and the supplier board reads beautifully with them. Two of the herb shots came back softer than the rest, which Ava reshot inside the revision round.
Zoe caught a compliance issue we had missed ourselves and fixed all three masters inside a day. Calm, precise, and the campaign film outperformed the last one.

Solid photography and the twilight exteriors are lovely, but two bedrooms were missing from the set and it took a dispute to settle it. Mateo was reasonable throughout and we would consider working together again on a smaller brief.
The showroom set is excellent and the storefront frame turned out to be sharp after all — that one was on us. Yuki was patient while we checked and the files are print-ready.

supportTickets.name: Ruth Kalu
supportTickets.subject: Usage rights before I post my first brief

supportTickets.name: Owen Bailey
supportTickets.subject: Can our dispute be held open while we wait for a part?
supportTickets.body: We have an open dispute about a missing demonstration film. The part needed to film it is on back order and we would rather wait for the film than take a refund. Can the case stay open for another two weeks?

replies.body: Yes — a case can stay open while both parties are working towards delivery, and the payment stays held in escrow the whole time. Could you confirm the expected date for the part so I can note it on the case?

supportTickets.name: Mateo Rossi
supportTickets.subject: Re-submitting a portfolio item after changes were requested
supportTickets.body: One of my venue films came back with changes requested. I have re-graded it and fixed the aspect ratio. Do I upload it as a new item or update the existing one so the review history stays together?

replies.body: Update the existing item and send it back for review — that keeps the whole history on one record, and the reviewer can see what changed. Uploading a new item starts the review from scratch and loses that context.
Perfect, updated and re-submitted. Thanks for the quick answer.
